findings.description: On the denial path, check() stores the refilled token count in bucket.tokens (line 69) but returns before updating bucket.updated_at (line 73 is only reached on success). The next call measures elapsed time from the old timestamp and adds the same refill again. Example with refill_rate 1/s: a bucket is drained at t=0; a cost-5 request at t=1 is denied, leaving tokens=1 with updated_at=0; at t=2 elapsed is 2 so tokens become 3 instead of 2. Repeated denied requests let clients accumulate tokens beyond the intended rate, so the limiter admits more traffic than configured.
findings.suggestion: Set bucket.updated_at = now before the denial return, e.g. move the assignment at line 73 above the `if bucket.tokens < cost` check.
findings.title: Denied token bucket requests refill tokens twice

findings.description: If cost is greater than capacity (for example, an expensive endpoint costing 5 with burst or limit set to 3), tokens can never reach cost because they are capped at capacity. Every such request is denied, and retry_after is computed as a finite wait that never leads to success. Clients honoring Retry-After retry forever. The middleware's default burst is `limit`, so this occurs whenever limit is below the expensive cost.
findings.suggestion: Reject or clamp requests where cost > capacity explicitly (for example raise ValueError or return a decision that signals the request can never be admitted), and validate configuration so that burst >= the maximum request cost.
findings.title: Requests whose cost exceeds burst can never succeed
